The compact MCP modes and chat limits have tests that use no network. The changes preserve the full MCP read modes. No source defect was found in this review.

1. `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs:27`: Resolve the conflict with current upstream main. Keep the current importer description and the new compact schemas. Run the required checks after the refresh.
2. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/ai_chat/worker.rs:219` and the PR body: Add before/after screenshots for the UI chat behavior. The review instructions require them for changes under `crates/ui`. Store the images only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. Link them from the PR body.
3. `crates/app/src/mcp/compact.rs:1` and the PR body, Tests: Supply the required heavy-lane results for the final head. Current upstream `AGENTS.md`, "Heavy lanes at review", requires them. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` selects the app heavy lanes (202 steps, including the build). The body reports only the quick gate and clippy. Run the reached lanes and record their results. These heavy tests were not run in this review; the dry run is not a pass.

Extra suites run:

None beyond the quick gate selection. The diff changes no fixture, golden, test data directory, or importer code. The extra fixture and importer rules do not select more suites.

Mutations and goldens:

The diff changes MCP read output and chat request limits. It changes no posted G-code, geometry algorithm, gouge check, collision check, or stock simulation. This is not a safety-tier review. No goldens moved. I did not repeat the author's mutation checks.

Requested before merge:

1. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/ai_chat/transport.rs:213`: Apply `ToolSet::Core` to the Prompt-JSON payload too. This branch ignores `set` and calls `prompt_context(project)`, which always includes the full tool registry. Thus the `Local Prompt-JSON` preset still sends 116 tool schemas. With an empty project, its system prompt contains 115,711 characters. The native core payload has 25 tools. This leaves the small local fallback model exposed to the context overflow that this PR must prevent. Preserve the confirmation instructions. Add an offline test that checks the Prompt-JSON payload as well as the native payload.

Extra suites run:

- An isolated Rust check copied the exact `build_tools_payload` function into `/tmp`. It linked the built app library and called `split_payload`. No PR file changed. Its assertion that both core payloads contain 25 tools failed, as follows:

```text
Native core tools: 25; Prompt-JSON core tools: 116; fallback system prompt characters: 115711; native wire tools in fallback: 0
assertion `left == right` failed: Local Prompt-JSON must honor ToolSet::Core
  left: 116
 right: 25
CHECK EXIT: 101
```

- The extra fixture and importer rules select no additional suite. The PR diff changes no fixture, golden, test data directory, or importer code.

Heavy lanes:

The body reports the app heavy targets on this PR head against upstream main `f85163b0ca948250fd6a51360d14754a282e0340`. The author reports 201 steps, 0 failed steps, 41 passed tests, and six expected failures in 45.2 minutes. The body names all six tests and issues #2845, #2849, and #1950. This supplies the evidence requested in the earlier review. I did not rerun the heavy tests. The current dry run still selects the app heavy targets; it is a plan, not a test pass.

Mutations and goldens:

The diff changes MCP read output and chat request limits. It changes no posted G-code, gouge check, collision check, stock simulation, or geometry algorithm. This is not a safety-tier review. No goldens moved. I did not repeat the author's mutations.

Notes:

A real provider endpoint was not exercised. The quick gate tests use offline transports for the chat changes. The new finding is in the Prompt-JSON payload selection, which the current core-set test does not cover.
